service.description: Out-parameters every Shopify extract returns (extract#ShopifyOrders, extract#ShopifyOrderLineUnits, extract#ShopifyOrderReturnRefs). A script service returns only declared out-parameters, so a result key added to an extract must be declared here.

In-parameters of the Bulk Operations window extracts (extract#ShopifyOrders, extract#ShopifyOrderLineUnits), which share submit, poll, download and file writing. None of them takes sourceFilters or filters at the read (DAR-BE-318): every record is written and Spark Keep (darpan core) sets aside what a run's rules reject.

parameter.description: Tenant-owned ShopifyAuthConfig identifier.

parameter.description: Automation id passed through for metadata.

parameter.name: fileSide

parameter.description: Source type identifier passed through for metadata.

parameter.description: Start of the automation window; accepts Timestamp, Date, ISO-8601 text, SQL timestamp text, or epoch milliseconds.

parameter.description: End of the automation window; accepts Timestamp, Date, ISO-8601 text, SQL timestamp text, or epoch milliseconds.

parameter.name: preserveWindowInstants
parameter.description: When true, treat windowStart and windowEnd as already normalized instants instead of reinterpreting UTC-midnight values through the Shopify config timezone.

parameter.name: windowStartDate
parameter.description: Raw parent window start passed by the automation executor.

parameter.name: windowEndDate
parameter.description: Raw parent window end passed by the automation executor.

parameter.description: Optional output directory. Defaults to runtime://datamanager/reconciliation-runs/{automationExecutionId}/{timestamp}/.

parameter.description: Optional observability run id for live extract progress. Accepted for dispatch-contract symmetry with the OMS extractor; Shopify progress emission (bulk-operation objectCount heartbeats) is a planned follow-up.

parameter.description: Optional expected total for progress percent. Accepted, not yet used.

parameter.description: HTTP connect timeout for Shopify GraphQL and Bulk Operations download requests.

parameter.name: readTimeoutMillis
parameter.description: HTTP read timeout for Shopify GraphQL and Bulk Operations download requests.

parameter.name: maxAttempts
parameter.description: Maximum attempts for retryable Shopify GraphQL transport failures.

parameter.description: Maximum Shopify Bulk Operations status polls before the extraction fails.

parameter.name: bulkPollIntervalMillis

parameter.name: bulkStartRetryAttempts
parameter.description: Number of retries when Shopify rejects the start request because another Bulk Operation is already running.

parameter.name: bulkStartRetryDelayMillis
parameter.description: Delay between Bulk Operation start retries when another operation is already running.

service.description: Extract Shopify orders for an automation window through Shopify Bulk Operations and write normalized JSON output to the automation data-manager folder.

parameter.name: lookupKeys
parameter.description: DAR-BE-156. Read these orders by legacy order id instead of the window (an audit re-checking its older open findings), LOOKUP_IDS_PER_BULK ids a bulk operation. The window parameters are still required but not used for the search.

parameter.name: windowFieldName
parameter.description: DAR-BE-318. Which order timestamp the window matches: createdAt (default, also when empty) or updatedAt (the kept copy's daily read of what changed). Any other value is refused. A read by key ignores it.

parameter.name: lookupKeyField
parameter.description: The record field lookupKeys name. Only the order id (id or legacyResourceId) is supported; any other field is refused.

parameter.name: withLineItems
parameter.description: DAR-BE-368. Also read each order's lines (id, SKU, name, quantity, current and unfulfilled quantity) as lineItems on the order, for an audit finding to show. Asked per check, through the automation source's parameters; off, the read is unchanged.

service.description: DAR-BE-318 (rulings P3b1-9, P3b1-13). The Shopify side of darpan's kept-copy projection for the return-refs events. A run's live read of these events rounds its window to whole days in the store's zone and widens it back by lookbackHours (3), which a slice of the copy cannot reproduce, so this refuses every side: it reads live. Named by the SHOPIFY_RETURN_REFS row (data/ShopifyConnectorSeedData.xml), so flipping that row's preserveWindowInstants to Y can never start serving a copy that lacks the lookback. Reads nothing.

set.value: the live read widens the window by its lookback and rounds it to whole days, which a slice of the copy cannot reproduce

service.description:
Extract Shopify order lines as ONE RECORD PER UNIT for the DAR-BE-050 Shopify-to-OMS unit presence pair, via a Bulk Operation over the orders connection filtered on created_at, writing normalized JSON output to the automation data-manager folder.
WHY UNITS AND NOT LINES: OMS explodes a Shopify line of quantity N into N single-unit OrderItems, and the Spark compare core is a left_anti join followed by .distinct() - set semantics. At line grain a line OMS imported SHORT still matches a complete Shopify line, so the pair reports clean on exactly the defect it exists to find. Each record carries a unitOrdinal and the compare key is (shopifyOrderId, shopifyLineId, unitOrdinal), matching extract#HotWaxOmsOrderLineUnits.
HOW IT DIFFERS FROM extract#ShopifyOrders: only the record-assembly step. It uses the SHOPIFY_ORDER_LINE_UNITS source, whose allowsBulkConnections opt-in lets lineItems into a bulk query; the resulting JSONL child lines are this extractor's records rather than something to be misread as orders. Bulk submit, poll, download and file writing are deliberately identical.
WINDOWING: created_at, matching the OMS side's orderDate. Changing one side only produces the DAR-BE-038 skew - structurally guaranteed false positives on every run.
orphanLineItemCount and droppedZeroQuantity are always present in requestMetadata, and an orphan also raises a run warning: a unit lost in assembly vanishes from the Shopify side, where the anti-join reports it as a genuine difference.
NO SOURCE FILTERS (DAR-BE-318): this service declares no sourceFilters parameter, so every assembled unit is written and Spark Keep (darpan core) sets aside what a run's rules reject (unitState, orderReturnStatus and the rest are ordinary unit fields to it). Dropping zero-quantity lines and orphan line items stays here: that is the shape of the unit grain, not a user rule.

parameter.name: recordCount
parameter.description: Number of UNITS written, not orders.

service.description:
Extract per-EVENT Shopify records for a window, for returns reconciliation against the OMS reconciliationReturns extract (DAR-BE-018). An event is a refund OR a return; this is the second reshape of this service's output — see ShopifyReturnRefsSupport's class doc (2026-08-17 returns-refund-grain-alignment plan, Task 1, REVISION 2026-08-18) for the full shape history.
Uses CURSOR pagination, not Bulk Operations: refunds and returns are GraphQL connections, and the bulk path rejects connection-bearing fields because bulk JSONL emits their children as separate __parentId lines that nothing here re-nests. That is why this service carries no bulk poll/retry parameters.
WINDOW SEMANTICS: this windows on the CREATION of each event itself, not on any order-level date (an order can be arbitrarily older than a refund or return on it). The Shopify search is a wide, lower-bound-only net (updated_at >= windowStart - lookbackHours, no upper bound, trimmed to orders that plausibly carry a refund or a return); [windowStart - lookbackHours, windowEnd) is then applied client-side against each refund's and each return's own createdAt independently. The lookback (default 3h) exists because OMS lags Shopify by ~38min (RQ-23): an OMS row just inside windowStart can point at a Shopify event created just before it, and that event must still be fetched for the OMS-side forward match to see it. See ShopifyReturnRefsSupport for the full rationale.
Each output record is one EVENT: {refundOrReturnId, refundOrReturnType, orderId, createdAt}, all ids bare (GID tail stripped) so they land in the same space as the OMS externalId. refundOrReturnType is "REFUND" or "RETURN". refundOrReturnId is the single join key OMS reconciliationReturns.externalId matches against — no precedence rule needed: the product owner confirmed (2026-08-18) that externalId is usually a Shopify refund id but sometimes a return id, and emitting both kinds as same-shaped rows under one refundOrReturnId column means whichever kind OMS actually used, the matching Shopify row is there to join against directly. This revision retires the refundId/returnId column split (and with it the refund-to-return association problem — see ShopifyReturnRefsSupport.toRecords for that investigation's history) and the earlier "no refund yet" warning: a return with no refund yet now emits its own RETURN row rather than being dropped.
REFUNDED-RETURN NARROWING (2026-08-18): a refunded return is represented by its REFUND row ALONE — the return itself does not also get a RETURN row, since the OMS-side contract (one row per return, one externalId field, stamped with the refund id once one exists — see ReturnPresenceVerificationSupport's class doc, "a refunded Shopify Return is never separately expected; its event is its refund") means a refunded return gets exactly ONE OMS counterpart, keyed by the refund id; a separate RETURN row for it would be a permanent, structural phantom missing-in-OMS. The discriminator is Return.refunds (a RefundConnection, confirmed present with no required args on every dated API version this catalog supports — not returns.nodes.status: that field was investigated first and REJECTED, since Shopify's own returnClose mutation doc confirms a return can reach CLOSED with zero refunds, and nothing prevents a refund existing while a return stays OPEN, so status cannot cleanly separate refunded from unrefunded returns in either direction. A return whose Return.refunds connection comes back empty gets its own RETURN row; any non-empty result means it is skipped. See ShopifyReturnRefsSupport.toRecords for the full rationale and evidence.
NO SOURCE FILTERS (DAR-BE-318): this service declares no sourceFilters parameter, so every event is written and Spark Keep (darpan core) sets aside what a run's rules reject. The field a rule is written against is orderReturnStatus, holding Shopify's own Order.returnStatus (IN_PROGRESS, INSPECTION_COMPLETE, NO_RETURN, RETURN_FAILED, RETURN_REQUESTED, RETURNED) on EVERY row, refunds included; excluding IN_PROGRESS therefore sets aside an in-progress order's REFUND rows too, and if OMS holds such a refund it will then report missing-in-Shopify. TWO DROPS STAY IN THE EXTRACTOR, ahead of any rule: a return that HAS a refund emits no RETURN row (2026-08-18), and a CLOSED return with NO refund emits none either (DAR-BE-027, counted in requestMetadata.filters.closedUnrefundedReturnsSuppressed, always present, zero included). The window floor is also widened by lookbackHours. None of these is a rule over a record field.
RETURN WORKFLOW STATUS (2026-08-27): RETURN rows also carry returnWorkflowStatus, the Shopify ReturnStatus of that return. It exists so operators can exclude in-progress returns (REQUESTED, OPEN) through the run's Keep rules (Spark Keep, DAR-BE-318) — a return the customer has merely opened has no OMS counterpart yet and would otherwise report as missing-in-OMS on every run until it completes. This is NOT a reversal of the narrowing above: Return.refunds remains the refunded/unrefunded discriminator, and this field is never read as one. It is deliberately NOT called returnStatus: Shopify's own Order.returnStatus is a DIFFERENT field with a different enum (OrderReturnStatus — IN_PROGRESS, INSPECTION_COMPLETE, NO_RETURN, RETURN_FAILED, RETURN_REQUESTED, RETURNED), an order-wide display aggregate, and the collision made operators exclude on values this field can never hold.

parameter.name: windowFieldName
parameter.description: DAR-BE-318. Which event timestamp the window matches: createdAt, the refund's or the return's own creation, which is what this read always windows on. Blank means the same. Any other value is refused, and so is a completedReturns read, which has no event date. Names the field so a kept copy of these events can be keyed and cut on it.

parameter.name: shopifyAuthConfigId
parameter.description: Tenant-owned Shopify auth config identifier.

parameter.name: automationExecutionId
parameter.description: Automation execution id used to choose the default data-manager output folder.

parameter.name: companyUserGroupId
parameter.description: Trusted automation owner tenant. When present, config access is checked against this tenant instead of a user-session active tenant.

parameter.name: fileName
parameter.description: Optional output file name. Defaults to shopify-return-refs-{fromMillis}-{thruMillis}.json.

parameter.name: pageSize
parameter.description: Orders per cursor page.

parameter.name: connectionPageSize
parameter.description: Refunds/returns fetched per order. Clamped to the ShopifySourceCatalog connectionMaxPageSize (100) regardless of the value requested here; truncation detection reads the clamped value back off the built query, not this raw parameter, so a warning still fires naming the order rather than silently truncating its id set. Also governs the nested per-return Return.refunds existence check (2026-08-18 narrowing) — it shares the same refunds connectionRoot/page-size as the order-level refunds list, since only emptiness of that nested connection is ever read, never its count.

parameter.name: completedReturns
parameter.description: DAR-BE-137. Set to read one row per ORDER with a return completed (CLOSED, closedAt in the window) instead of refund/return events: "refunded" keeps orders whose completed return has a refund, "exchanged" orders whose completed return has exchange items, "orderRefunded" (DAR-CLIENT-005) orders whose completed return was refunded on the return or on the order on or after the return was made (RAILS's Loop refunds the order and never links the refund to the Return). For a tenant whose returns are checked against NetSuite (Dolls Kill, RAILS). Rows carry orderId, orderName (no leading #), returnIds, returnCount, closedAt and originalUnfulfilledQuantity (the order's own lines Shopify has not fulfilled, leaving out the lines an exchange added: an exchange reaches NetSuite only once its original order is fulfilled), and (DAR-BE-359) the order's orderDate, displayFinancialStatus, displayFulfillmentStatus, totalPrice, currencyCode and totalRefunded; lookbackHours does not apply.

parameter.name: lookbackHours
parameter.description: Hours the fetch/emit floor is widened BEFORE windowStart, so a Shopify event created just before windowStart is still available for the OMS-side forward match (OMS lags Shopify by ~38min, RQ-23). Does not change the reporting window itself — matches ReturnPresenceVerificationSupport.DEFAULT_GRACE_HOURS in the darpan component by default.

service.description: Point-existence check for Shopify refund/return ids against the primary datastore via nodes(ids:). The returns extract must enumerate through orders(query:) because the Admin API has no top-level refunds or returns connection, and that search-index-backed net was observed to omit old orders carrying new refunds — so the saved-run verification pass calls this to confirm or refute "missing in SHOPIFY" differences for the returns pair. The id's type is not known to the caller, so each bare id is checked under BOTH the Refund and Return gid forms and counted present if either resolves. A failed lookup returns ok=false with both id lists empty — it never classifies an id as missing.

parameter.name: refundOrReturnIds
parameter.description: Shopify refund OR return ids to check; bare numeric ids, or gid://shopify/Refund/... / gid://shopify/Return/... values. A bare id is checked under both forms.

service.description: Point-existence check for Shopify order ids against the primary datastore via nodes(ids:). The bulk extraction's orders(query:) filter is served by Shopify's search index, which can omit a small number of real orders; the saved-run verification pass calls this to confirm or refute "missing in SHOPIFY" differences. A failed lookup returns ok=false with both id lists empty — it never classifies an order as missing.

parameter.name: orderIds
parameter.description: Shopify order ids to check; numeric ids or gid://shopify/Order/... values.

service.description: Enumerate exchanges created in Shopify whose return date falls inside the run window (product contract 2026-07-31: every Shopify exchange must have been imported into OMS). Sweeps updated_at with no upper bound and filters Return.createdAt client-side. Requires the read_returns scope. A failed sweep returns ok=false with an empty list — it never classifies anything.
